text.p: West Australian Newspapers Ltd chairman Trevor Eastwood on Thursday challenged two institutional shareholders to either seek board seats or sell their stock in a squabble over the issue of executive shares.

Eastwood told the company's annual meeting in Perth that the State Authorities Superannuation Board, which holds 2.98 percent of the newspaper publisher, and Tower Life, which holds 0.8 percent, had lodged proxies against a motion to award shares managing director Denis Thompson.

The share issue was proposed for all staff but because Thompson is a director a special resolution with 75 percent support was required to approve the issue to him. Eastwood said the motion had received 80 percent approval through proxies.
"It is disappointing to note that two of our top 20 shareholders have lodged proxies to vote against this motion," Eastwood said.
"They have done this without making any attempt to contact the board and explain their views or attempt to seek the view of your directors on this matter," he said.

"I believe this to be an irresponsible use of power on their part and as remuneration of the chief executive is one of the major responsibilities of the board it is tantamount to a vote of no confidence in the board," Eastwood said.
"Those shareholders should look to replace the board with one of similar views to themselves or leave the register."

Eastwood said one of the major roles of a board of directors was to select the chief executive, work with him in setting the corporate objectives, and monitor his and thus the whole company's performance.

"In addition the board has the responsibility to set the remuneration of the chief executive and structure that remuneration in such a way that the chief executive's interests are aligned with those of the shareholders," he said.
In 1992 shareholders approved a staff share plan whereby the board of directors could issue up to five percent of the company's ordinary shares to the employees of the group.
To date the company has issued about three percent of the company's ordinary shares to employees.
After the latest issue, a total of 3.8 percent of the company's shares will have been issued under the plan.
